faq.q: How will AI change office politics?
faq.a: AI makes proof, information access and testing cheap, so authority built on delayed results and information silos becomes harder to sustain.

faq.q: What is the difference between performative and pragmatic AI use?
faq.a: Performative use manufactures the appearance of progress, such as prettier decks and dashboards. Pragmatic use runs real experiments, validates data and ships working tools.

geoRationale: The piece has a strong, extractable thesis and a clear two-way contrast (Truth Seekers vs Political Players; performative vs pragmatic), which suits answer engines. Weaknesses are that headings are statements rather than the questions readers ask, key terms (Truth Seekers, Political Players) are not defined in one citable sentence near the top, and there are no named sources or concrete examples, so the factual density is low. Recommendations: add a one-sentence definition of the core thesis in the opening, convert one or two headings to question form, add one specific sourced example, and link to the long version. Draft issues observed: title begins lowercase 'the', numbered headings mix title case ('Death of cheap authority'), and the opening has grammar slips ('used to see', 'proof much delayed') that undermine extractable quotes and should be fixed by the editorial agent. The intake gate G1 also flags a banned term and a long sentence, which are not re-litigated here. All of this is recommendation only: no search volumes, rankings or AI citation outcomes were measured, and no technique guarantees inclusion in AI answers. Keep the short and long versions distinct in angle or canonicalise to one.
